messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager fired: `kv_cache_eviction_alert` in prod-central. Eviction ratio > 20% over 4m, correlated with p99 latency spikes on short-tail generation routes.

alex: i'm oncall. seeing increased 429/503 on /v1/generate for a subset of tenants. Priya, can you pull per-pool eviction and hit-rate?

priya: running queries now. Top affected pool: g4-pool-11 (nodes 21-24). eviction_rate ~0.22, hit_rate dropped to ~0.62. Prefix-heavy tenants: tenant:neo/* and tenant:flux/* showing biggest growth in prefix count.

jorge: any recent deploys touching metadata or prefix encoding?

emma: support reports a deploy about 1.5h ago that adjusted request metadata serialization. Noted in deploy message but assumed harmless.

priya: quick correlate with deploys: yes, commit b7f2a8 adjusted metadata batch keys. rolling window started then.

alex: immediate mitigation options: 1) emergency bump kvcache.max_entries on g4-pool-11 nodes; 2) short TTL for prefix entries to age them out; 3) temporarily redirect heavy tenants to alternate pool with more capacity. Low blast is 2.

jorge: redirecting tenants is risky. Let's do a conservative bump on each node and enable per-prefix TTL at 5m for the pool for 30m window. I'll roll node-21 first for a test.

ops-bot: Creating silence for `kv_cache_eviction_alert` on prod-central for 40m as requested by alex.

ops-bot: Silence created by alex: `kv_cache_eviction_alert` duration 40m.

jorge: applied kvcache.max_entries=2200000 on g4-node-21 and set per-prefix ttl override to 300s for pool g4-pool-11. Monitoring.

priya: node-21 eviction dropped 21% -> 6.8% in 2m, p99 latency for short-gen down ~140ms. Rolling nodes 22-24 now via orchestration job `ops rollout kvcache-config --pool g4-pool-11 --nodes 21-24 --max 2200000 --ttl 300`.

alex: good. Emma, please prepare customer comms for tenants we saw errors for. Mark severity: degraded throughput, not data loss.

emma: drafting messages. Will queue to affected tenants and CSMs. Ticket created: INC-2041.

priya: long-term monitoring changes proposed: current alert is too sensitive to transient spikes. My proposal: switch to two-tier alerts: (A) sustained eviction per-pool > 10% for 6m => page; (B) eviction > 7% for 4m combined with p95 latency increase > 20% => page. Also add alert labels for pool/tenant and only page if pool in owned list. Finally, add a suppression rule so we don't page when cluster_mem_util > 0.90 (we'll treat node-level memory pressure differently).

alex: sounds good. Please draft Prometheus rules and tests.

priya: draft rules (sketch):
```
- alert: KVCacheEvictionSustained
  expr: (sum by(pool) (increase(kvcache_evictions_total{env=\"prod\"}[6m]))
         / sum by(pool) (increase(kvcache_lookups_total{env=\"prod\"}[6m]))) > 0.10
  for: 6m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/kvcache-runbook

- alert: KVCacheEvictionLatencyCombo
  expr: ((sum by(pool)(increase(kvcache_evictions_total{env=\"prod\"}[4m]))
         / sum by(pool)(increase(kvcache_lookups_total{env=\"prod\"}[4m]))) > 0.07)
        and (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{env=\"prod\"}[4m])) by (le)) > (1.2 * avg_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{env=\"prod\"}[1h])) by (le))[1h:])))
  for: 4m
```

priya: also proposing Grafana panels: per-pool eviction_rate, hit_rate, mem_utilization, per-tenant prefix_count as heatmap. Queries: 
```
- eviction_rate: sum by(pool)(rate(kvcache_evictions_total[1m])) / sum by(pool)(rate(kvcache_lookups_total[1m]))
- hit_rate: sum by(pool)(rate(kvcache_hits_total[1m])) / sum by(pool)(rate(kvcache_lookups_total[1m]))
- prefix_count: max by(tenant, pool)(kvcache_prefix_count)
```

jorge: need instrumentation: kvcache exporter should emit prefix_count gauge and prefix_size_bytes histogram. I'll PR exporter changes.

priya: please include tenant label so we can slice by customer. We also want a per-prefix size distribution for heatmap panels.

ops-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/monitoring/pull/947 (adds new alerts + test fixtures) by priya.

jorge: opened exporter PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kvcache-exporter/pull/58 (adds prefix_size_bytes histogram and prefix_count gauge). Assigning to priya for review.

alex: timeline: emergency mitigation rolled in 12m, cluster stable in ~28m. We'll document this in the incident timeline and create follow-ups for runbook and canary.

emma: follow-ups created: DOC-470 (update kvcache runbook with TTL override steps), TASK-900 (prefix-count canary + quota enforcement), MON-3010 (Grafana heatmap + dashboard pin). Assignments: jorge/priya/emma.

priya: merging PR 947 once tests pass. I'll add the squelch condition for cluster_mem_util > 0.90 to avoid misfires when memory pressure is global.

ops-bot: Incident recorded: duration 34m. Root cause: metadata serialization change increased per-request prefix load → cache pressure → evictions → latency. Mitigations: emergency cache size bump and temporary per-prefix TTL, alert rule overhaul, exporter instrumentation, dashboard creation.

alex: handing over to next oncall @jorge-night for 8h monitoring. Please keep an eye on newly added panels and the per-tenant heatmap; if any tenant shows sudden prefix growth, pause deploys and throttle metadata writes.

jorge-night: taking it. Will monitor KV panels and be reachable via DMs for urgent issues.

support-bot: Status page updated: Partial Service Degradation in prod-central during incident window. Customer notifications sent.

alex: thanks team — clean mitigation and good coordination. Logging off.
